links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 responses on IR procedure complications (FKGL, FRE, SMOG)
links.effect: Mean FKGL 12.51 ± 1.14, Flesch Reading Ease 30.27 ± 8.38, SMOG 14.46 ± 0.76, all college level; no difference between vascular and non-vascular (p = 0.16).
links.quote: The mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease scores, and SMOG index were 12.51 ± 1.14 (college level) 30.27 ± 8.38 (college level), and 14.46 ± 0.76 (college level), respectively.

links.outcome: Comprehensibility of AI-generated patient information on procedure complications
links.effect: Readability was overall low at college level; a high level of education and health literacy is required to comprehend responses.
links.quote: Based on the findings of our study, while ChatGPT provides accurate information and shows no evidence of hallucinations, it is important to emphasize that a high level of education and health literacy are required to fully comprehend its responses.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT-4 responses regarding interventional radiology procedural complications without testing a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
